name: Binary Exploitation & Reverse Engineering
tagline: Debug, disassemble, decompile, and understand binaries — your own code, lab targets, and CTF challenges.

tools.name: Ghidra
tools.desc: Free software reverse-engineering suite with a GUI and a real decompiler that emits C-like pseudocode, plus a scriptable Python/Java API.
tools.when: Full static analysis of binaries you own or CTF challenges — the decompiler output reads far closer to source than raw disassembly.
tools.install: Download the release zip from the Ghidra releases page, unzip, and run ./ghidraRun

tools.name: IDA Free
tools.desc: Hex-Rays' freeware edition of IDA, a mature interactive disassembler with decompiler support for x86/x64/ARM and a plugin ecosystem.
tools.when: A free, officially supported disassembler when you prefer IDA's workflow for x86/x64 binaries over the Ghidra GUI.

tools.name: Binary Ninja
tools.desc: Commercial reverse-engineering platform with a modern Python API, cross-platform analysis, and both an interactive GUI and headless mode.
tools.when: Scriptable binary analysis with an expressive API, or when team licensing matches your lab workflow.

tools.name: radare2
tools.desc: Command-line reverse-engineering framework with built-in analyzer, disassembler, ESIL emulation, and scripting via r2pipe.
tools.when: Headless or scripted analysis, quick on-box triage, and when the whole analysis pipeline should live in one terminal tool.

tools.name: rizin
tools.desc: Actively maintained fork of radare2 aiming for a cleaner, better-tested codebase while staying command-compatible and offering rz-pipe bindings.
tools.when: Same CLI workflow as radare2 when you prefer the fork under active development for its language bindings and released packages.

tools.name: Cutter
tools.desc: Qt GUI built on the Rizin engine giving point-and-click disassembly, patching, control-flow graphs, and a decompiler view.
tools.when: Visual exploration and annotation of binaries without a terminal-heavy workflow.

tools.name: GhidraSnippets
tools.desc: Curated Python and Java snippets for the Ghidra scripting API covering common auto-analysis, function, and disassembly tasks.
tools.when: Steal working, tested Ghidra script patterns instead of re-deriving the API for each new analysis task.

tools.name: ghidra-scripts
tools.desc: Maintained collection of Ghidra Python scripts for pattern-based analysis, function identification, and decompiler querying.
tools.when: Drop-in automation scripts for reversing binaries or firmware in an iterative lab analysis session.

tools.name: r2ghidra
tools.desc: Plugin that embeds the Ghidra decompiler into radare2/rizin so terminal workflows gain C-like pseudocode output.
tools.when: Bring a decompiler view into your radare2/rizin session without switching to the Ghidra GUI.

tools.name: GDB
tools.desc: GNU debugger supporting breakpoints, watchpoints, register and memory inspection, and scripting for ELF, PE, and Mach-O binaries.
tools.when: The backbone of all dynamic work; run it plain for minimalism or host pwndbg/GEF on top of it.

tools.name: pwndbg
tools.desc: GDB plugin with exploit-focused conveniences: heap/stack views, ROP-gadget search, cyclic pattern generation, and prettier disassembly.
tools.when: CTF pwn challenges or reversing binaries you own when plain GDB layout gets too noisy.

tools.name: GEF
tools.desc: Dependency-light, single-script GDB plugin with heap visualizations, format-string helpers, and live memory introspection.
tools.when: A pwndbg-style workflow with almost zero setup beyond one curl command, on any GDB build.

tools.name: LLDB
tools.desc: LLVM's debugger, well integrated with clang-generated debug info and Mach-O, Swift, and Objective-C symbols.
tools.when: Analyzing Apple-platform binaries or anything built with the LLVM toolchain where GDB support lags.

tools.name: Frida
tools.desc: Dynamic instrumentation toolkit that injects JavaScript into a running process to hook functions and read live memory without recompiling.
tools.when: Trace calls, intercept functions, or inspect a live process — especially on targets where a traditional debugger struggles.

tools.name: strace / ltrace
tools.desc: Syscall and library-call tracers that log every system call (or libc call) a process makes, with arguments and timing.
tools.when: Map a binary's runtime behavior by watching the syscalls it issues during a controlled run on your host.

tools.name: QEMU
tools.desc: Full-system and user-mode emulator running and tracing binaries for foreign architectures, with a GDB remote stub.
tools.when: Execute and debug cross-architecture ELF (ARM, MIPS, PPC) from firmware or CTFs when no native hardware exists.

tools.name: Qiling
tools.desc: Advanced binary emulation framework that runs and instruments cross-architecture binaries inside a controlled Python sandbox.
tools.when: Automated, scripted emulation of cross-platform binaries with hooks, memory inspection, and reproducible lab runs.

tools.name: Unicorn
tools.desc: Lightweight CPU emulator framework exposing per-instruction hooks so you can emulate only the instruction flow you care about.
tools.when: Embed instruction-level emulation into your own analysis or fuzzing scripts for lab targets.

tools.name: pwntools
tools.desc: CTF pwn toolkit providing packing (p64/u64), ELF parsing, cyclic patterns, ROP-chain builders, and managed local/remote I/O.
tools.when: Prototype and test exploit behavior against binaries in a lab or CTF — the standard glue for the whole workflow.

tools.name: angr
tools.desc: Python binary analysis framework using symbolic/concolic execution to explore paths and solve constraints against a binary you control.
tools.when: Automated pathfinding — such as deriving inputs that satisfy checks — when manual reversing is too slow.

tools.name: ROPgadget
tools.desc: Scans binaries for return-oriented-programming gadgets and can dump the full gadget set or filter specific instructions.
tools.when: Collect usable ROP gadgets from a stripped binary you own before assembling a chain.

tools.name: Ropper
tools.desc: Python tool to inventory ROP gadgets and build chains from ELF, PE, and Mach-O binaries; powers gadget search inside pwndbg.
tools.when: Quick gadget inventory across multiple binary formats in a lab when auditing which sequences are constructible.

tools.name: one_gadget
tools.desc: Matches libc builds to single-address execve('/bin/sh') gadgets whose register constraints are simple to satisfy.
tools.when: You have a libc build in a lab or CTF and want short candidate gadget addresses before scripting the constraints.

tools.name: Z3
tools.desc: Microsoft's SMT solver used to solve constraints over bitvectors, powering automated deobfuscation and input recovery.
tools.when: Solve the arithmetic and bitvector equations that symbolic execution or manual analysis hands you.

tools.name: Speculator
tools.desc: IBM Research framework to analyze speculative-execution attacks (ret2spec/spectre class) and their mitigations across architectures.
tools.when: Academic-lab study of ret2spec-family microarchitectural attacks and how current mitigations cover them.

tools.name: Retbleed PoC
tools.desc: Research proof-of-concept from the ret2spec lineage demonstrating arbitrary speculative code execution via return instructions.
tools.when: Reproduce published speculative-execution research artifacts in a lab to measure the impact of mitigations.

tools.name: Capstone
tools.desc: Disassembly engine that decodes raw bytes into platform-pinned instructions for many architectures, usable from Python, C, and more.
tools.when: Programmatically decode instruction streams inside your own scripts, emulators, or plugin code.

tools.name: Keystone
tools.desc: Assembly engine that turns mnemonics into machine code at runtime, complementing Capstone for code generation.
tools.when: Assemble shellcode or encoding routines on the fly inside your own lab scripts and tooling.

tools.name: checksec
tools.desc: Bash/Python script that reads ELF headers and reports active mitigations: PIE, NX, canaries, RELRO, Fortify, and more.
tools.when: First move on any binary in a lab or CTF — establish the mitigation baseline before choosing deeper tooling.

tools.name: file
tools.desc: Identifies a file's type from magic bytes, including format and target architecture (e.g. ELF 64-bit x86-64).
tools.when: Instant triage of any unknown artifact to confirm what you are looking at before deeper analysis.

tools.name: strings
tools.desc: Prints printable character sequences from a binary, exposing embedded literals, format strings, and library references without executing it.
tools.when: Grab a quick inventory of interesting strings — prompts, /bin/sh, format specifiers — before disassembling.

tools.name: objdump / readelf
tools.desc: binutils disassembler and ELF reader providing symbol tables, sections, headers, dynamic imports, and per-arch disassembly.
tools.when: Zero-dependency static lookups — grep symbols, inspect section layout, or dump disassembly without a full RE suite.

tools.name: Diaphora
tools.desc: Binary diffing tool matching functions across two binaries and importing names and symbols, working with Ghidra, IDA, and Binary Ninja.
tools.when: Compare patched vs unpatched firmware or file versions to spot the instruction-level changes behind a fix.
